entities.summary: Remarks on Frazer's Golden Bough is a collection of Ludwig Wittgenstein's thoughts on James George Frazer's The Golden Bough: A Study in Magic and Religion. The commentary was initially published in 1967, with an English edition in 1979. Wittgenstein wrote the text in the summer of 1931. It represented his earliest efforts to compose what became the Philosophical Investigations (1953). An important theme of the Remarks, and one which Wittgenstein later explored more fully, is the conception of metaphysics as a "kind of magic".
